beats.narration_text: Vanakkam — this is Liam, in for Komal. Camera traps never sleep. Most of what they catch is empty woods. Today: what AI actually does for a conservatory at scale, how a detector is not a species name, and one open model already boxing animals so people stop clicking blanks.

beats.narration_text: Why this is live now. A single study can run hundreds of cameras for months. That is millions of images. Most of them are empty — wind, leaves, a temperature swing. A trained reviewer can clear a few hundred frames an hour. A million-image pile is weeks before any science starts.

shot.prompt: Empty infrared camera-trap frame — the bottleneck, not a species.

beats.narration_text: What it changed for operations. The first job is not naming the animal. It is skipping the blanks. Filter the empties, and the review queue shrinks by about an order of magnitude. Less clicking. More conservation.

shot.prompt: Contact sheet of camera-trap frames — mostly empty, a few animals.

beats.narration_text: Start with names. Detect: is there an animal, a person, a vehicle. Classify: which species. Identify: which individual — that is Wildbook, a different machine, already on this channel. Those are not synonyms.

beats.narration_text: Worked example. MegaDetector. Open-source, from Microsoft's A.I. for Good Lab. It boxes animals, people, and vehicles in camera-trap images. It does not name the species. You set a threshold, skip the blanks, and a person still reviews. Always test it on your own data.

shot.prompt: USFWS trail-camera deer with a teaching overlay: animal, not a species name.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Camera traps never sleep. Most frames are empty. Detect is not classify is not identify. MegaDetector boxes what is there so people stop clicking blanks. Design judgment: if it names the species, it is not this detector. Ask what a missed animal would cost.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude with a folder you actually have — camera-trap frames, drone stills, a conservatory backlog. (1) Detect, classify, or identify — which machine is running? (2) What share of the pile is empty, and who still reviews? (3) What would a missed animal cost in that field? Score the system: a filter at scale, or a smarter ranger. Run it before the next survey season.
